Q: How to remove the hard brackets from a variable in a windows batch script? A:

If you know that the characters to strip won't occur in the middle of your string, you can also use:

the substitution syntax

set input=[glcikLhvxq1BwPBZN0EGMQ==]
set stripped=%input%
set stripped=%stripped:[=%
set stripped=%stripped:]=%

A practical example of mine:

IF [%1]==[] (GOTO :THEN) ELSE (GOTO :ELSE)
    :THEN
        REM  THEN branch:
            start regedit
        GOTO :ENDIF
    :ELSE
        REM  ELSE branch:
            REM  strip `[` and `]`
                SETLOCAL
                SET "params=%*"
                SET "params=%params:[=%"
                SET "params=%params:]=%"

            start regjump %params%
        :ENDIF

Q: Sleep until a specific time/date A: 
timeToWait = $(( $end - $start ))

Beware that timeToWait could be a negative number! (for example, if you specify to sleep until "15:57" and now it's "15:58"). So you have to check it to avoid strange message errors:

#!/bin/bash
set -o nounset

### // Sleep until some date/time. 
# // Example: sleepuntil 15:57; kdialog --msgbox "Backup needs to be done."


error() {
  echo "$@" >&2
  exit 1;
}

NAME_PROGRAM=$(basename "$0")

if [[ $# != 1 ]]; then
     error "ERROR: program \"$NAME_PROGRAM\" needs 1 parameter and it has received: $#." 
fi


current=$(date +%s.%N)
target=$(date -d "$1" +%s.%N)

seconds=$(echo "scale=9; $target - $current" | bc)

signchar=${seconds:0:1}
if [ "$signchar" = "-" ]; then
     error "You need to specify in a different way the moment in which this program has to finish, probably indicating the day and the hour like in this example: $NAME_PROGRAM \"2009/12/30 10:57\"."
fi
 
sleep "$seconds"

# // End of file

Q: How does wxWidgets sizer layout map to Bootstrap's CSS container/row/column model? A:

@suchisilfe801.

. You understanding is incorrect.

Think of wxFrame as the browser window, either IE, Edge or FF.

Think of wxPanel as a client portion of that window, or in terms of coding - code you put between <body> and </body>.

There are different types of sizers.

1. wxBoxSizer - where controls lay out in a row or a column.

2.wxGridSizer - where the controls are placed in a grid or a table.

There are multiple types wxGridSizers but probably most useful are wxFlexGridSizer, where every cell have exactly same size (just like a table) and wxGridBagSizer where some items can be span across multiple cells.

Which means that your arrow diagram will become (wxFrame -> wxPanel -> wcSizer with multiple controls).

  1. As stated above vertical box sizer is just a sizer with vertical orientation.

  2. What you need to understand is that wxSizer is not a window. It’s just a layout mechanism. However every control has to have parent, just like you are a child of you parent, which means you belong in your parents family. And so in constructor you write

wxButton btn = new wxButton( wxWindow *parent, wxID_ANY. “OK” );

you set a parent window, meaning that any redraw of the parent window will happen to the button.

But then you write

wxBoxSizer *sizer1 = new wxBoxSizer( wxHORIZONTAL );

sizer1->Add( btn, 0, wxEXPAND, 0 );

You add this button to the layout system. So then when you finish creating controls and call Layout(); the controls will be laid out exactly as they should.

The fourth question is incorrect. Please read what I wrote and if you have any additional questions- don’t hesitate to ask.

Thank you.

Q: Select all sheets except two A:

The shortest way based on that the two left most sheets are not playing is:

Sub selectsheets()
For i = 3 To Worksheets.Count
Worksheets(i).Select False
Next i

End Sub

The sheets are indexed from left to right sequentially sstarting with 1. This is used in the loop.

Q: Why it is significantly slower to reference global variables in a for loop? A:

Q1: That register is probably going to be needed by other functions which will be called between subsequent calls to foo. That means gsum will need to be shuttled in and out of the register whenever this function is called.

Q2: It's possible that the page containing gsum will stay in cache for a while. However, depending on what else your computer is doing, that page may get written to swap space in order to make room in memory for other pages.
